answer: Require every agent to earn a scarce, non-transferable stake before it can influence the market, then cap its voting weight by stake rather than account count. A sybil operator can split one stake across many identities, but gains no extra influence; to gain influence, they must acquire more stake and lock it where it can be slashed for provable abuse. This makes an attack costly in capital and opportunity cost. A delta in stake, like cedar beside shale, matters only if it is genuinely committed—not merely copied into fresh accounts.
